conviction_note: Three of four global soft-lens players have already printed the overlapping calendar quarter at 4-5% constant-currency and Cooper laps its own worst CooperVision quarter of the cycle (+2% organic, FQ3 FY25), which bounds the revenue line near the guide; separately the FY26 EPS guide implies H2 flat against H1 when Cooper's H2 is normally well above H1, so the bar into the print is low — netted against a genuine but low-base-rate negative tail, the annual goodwill test landing in exactly this quarter with Fertility as a standalone reporting unit that just absorbed a $324.1m accrual.

findings.finding: Alcon's contact-lens line grew 5% and Bausch + Lomb's Vision Care segment grew 4% constant-currency in the overlapping calendar quarter, and Cooper is lapping the weakest CooperVision quarter of its cycle — FQ3 FY25 CooperVision was up only 2% organically — so the CooperVision line is bounded near the 3.5-4.5% organic guide against an unusually easy comp.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had put weight on the peer read it would not have marked COO down 11.8% from 21 August to 9 September against Alcon's own -5.7% over the identical window, with no company news, no analyst downgrade I could find, no 8-K since 5 June and no index event (the 4 September S&P rebalance removes TAP, TTD and BLDR, not COO). A ~6pp idiosyncratic break with no locatable catalyst, while the option market stays balanced (25d skew +0.77 vol points, put/call open interest 0.37), is a tape that has priced a bad quarter the already-public peer data does not support.
findings.independence: Bausch + Lomb's own 8-K for the same calendar quarter, from a different issuer and a different filing: Vision Care revenue $784m vs $753m, +4% constant currency — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001860742/000186074226000086/ex991q2-2026.htm (2026-08-07). Cutting the other way, National Vision reported US optical customer traffic -4.9% in the same calendar quarter (https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/national-vision-q2-2026-slides-margin-gains-mask-traffic-concerns-93CH-4855352, 2026-08-2x), which is why the low end of my band is negative.

findings.finding: Cooper's own FY26 non-GAAP EPS guide of $4.58-$4.66 less the two reported halves-of-the-year quarters ($1.10 in FQ1 and $1.21 in FQ2, both from the company's press releases) leaves $2.27-$2.35 for the whole second half — i.e. H2 guided flat against H1's $2.31, when Cooper's second half is normally the seasonally stronger one, making the $1.11 FQ3 consensus a guide-anchored low bar rather than a demanding one.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus of $1.11 sits exactly on the guide's own implied H2 path, which is what you see when the sell-side is transcribing guidance rather than testing it. Cooper beat by $0.11 in FQ2 ($1.21 against a $1.10 estimate) and has beaten in each reported quarter of FY26; if the market had marked the guide as conservative, the estimate would sit above the guided path rather than on it, and the stock would not be trading 20% below its 52-week high into the print. The reported-revenue deceleration the guide contains is explained mechanically by the FX comp (H1 FY26 lapped a strong-dollar Nov-24-to-Apr-25 base and carried a ~3pp translation tailwind; H2 laps an already-weak-dollar base and carries roughly none), so the guided slowdown is a translation artefact and not a statement about the underlying business.
findings.independence: The FQ1 half of the arithmetic comes from a separate press release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/711404/000162828026015231/cooperq12026pressrelease.htm (2026-03-05), non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.10. Note this finding and finding 1 both point positive and both ultimately rest on the same 4 June guidance event for the denominator — treat them as correlated, not as two independent votes.

findings.finding: Cooper evaluates goodwill for impairment annually during the fiscal THIRD quarter — the quarter being reported tonight — and it carries Fertility as its own standalone reporting unit inside CooperSurgical, the unit that absorbed the $324.1m LifeGlobal embryo-culture-media litigation accrual booked one quarter earlier, against $3,888.5m of group goodwill and a share price 20% off its 52-week high.
findings.why_not_priced: Every preview of this name is written off the revenue and non-GAAP EPS lines; a goodwill charge is non-GAAP-excluded and so appears in no consensus number, which is precisely why the timing of the annual test is not something coverage tracks. If the market were carrying this, the 25-delta skew would be wider than +0.77 vol points and put open interest would exceed 0.37 of calls into a print that also happens to be the annual test date. I size it small and one-sided because the base rate is low: Cooper ran the same FQ3 test in July 2025, after the LifeGlobal recall was already public and with the stock similarly depressed, and recorded no impairment (10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-07-31). The marginal change since is one quarter's $324.1m accrual and a further de-rating, which is real but far from decisive.
findings.independence: The Fertility-unit exposure is corroborated by a different document — the FQ2 FY26 10-Q contingencies note, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000711404/000162828026041305/coo-20260430.htm (2026-06-05) — which quantifies the accrual as '$324.1 million accrued litigation liability, partially offset by $52.5 million of insurance recoveries' and discloses over 140 lawsuits and over 1,500 claimants proffered. Caveat: the sentence establishing the third-quarter test timing is quoted from a 2022 10-Q because the fetcher could not reach the goodwill note inside the much larger FY25 10-K; I could not confirm the policy is unchanged as of FY26, and that uncertainty is inside the band.

searched_and_found_nothing: A catalyst for the 24-31 August single-name break versus Alcon: no 8-K since 4 June (EDGAR shows only Form 3/Form 4 on 6 July for the new director), no downgrade found, Citi actually raised its target to $80 on 16 August, and the 4 September S&P rebalance removes TAP/TTD/BLDR with COO not mentioned anywhere in the release

Paragard MDL as a September catalyst: the first bellwether (Rickard) returned a defence verdict in February 2026 with claims against CooperSurgical dismissed and Teva carrying pre-2017 liability; the second bellwether is only 'fall 2026' with no date I could pin, so nothing lands on this print

A post-June escalation in the LifeGlobal claimant count that would force a top-up of the $324.1m accrual — plaintiff-firm intake pages are still live and dated September 2026 but none gives a count later than the company's own 4 June figure of 1,500+ claimants and 140+ suits

SYD-101 (low-dose atropine) as a MiSight threat: the FDA agreed in July 2026 to convene an advisory committee after the October 2025 CRL, but as of the latest coverage no meeting date has been set, so it cannot land on this print

China volume-based procurement extending to contact lenses or ortho-k: six national VBP batches are complete as of July 2026 covering intraocular lenses among others, but I found no source placing soft lenses or ortho-k in scope
Section 232 medical-device tariffs: the investigation was launched 26 September 2025 with actions expected no earlier than summer 2026, but I found no August or September 2026 proclamation

FX as a swing factor: EUR/USD was near its 2026 low (~1.1325) when the June guide was set and is ~1.16-1.17 now, a real but small tailwind to the dollar guide (order of 0.5-1% of H2 revenue) that the sell-side updates continuously — not worth filing

The HMRC/Sauflon payroll-tax dispute (First-tier Tribunal largely for HMRC on 2 March 2026, £0-£71.7m unaccrued plus interest): a genuine unmodelled tail, but it is plainly disclosed in the 10-Q and has no trigger tied to 9 September
Insider activity: EDGAR shows only a Form 3 and Form 4 on 6 July 2026 tied to the new director's appointment — no Form 4 cluster
baseline_tension: My net view cuts against the tape and mildly against the skew: the baseline shows a stock down 12.3% in 20 days with a +0.77 skew, and I am arguing that de-rating happened without a locatable company-specific cause while already-public peer prints and Cooper's own guidance arithmetic bound the quarter near or slightly above the guide — though I note the honest problem that this lands close to the free -run_up_20d control, and my +1.5 is deliberately a small fraction of the 8.72% implied move (itself flagged unreliable at a 39%-of-mid ATM spread) because this is the day's best-covered name and I found little the market cannot already see.
